LLM auditresponse for standard-path-mupdf-build.patch:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a simple upstream qmake build-config patch (`pdf_viewer_build_config.pro`) used to make sioyek build against a system-installed mupdf instead of a bundled/embedded copy. The only change is in the `unix:!mac` / `CONFIG(linux_app_image)` block: it adds `DEFINES += LINUX_STANDARD_PATHS` and replaces the bundled link line (`-Lmupdf/build/release -lmupdf -lmupdf-third -lmupdf-threads -lharfbuzz -lz`) with a plain `LIBS += -ldl -lmupdf -lz`.

This is ordinary distro/packaging adaptation — dropping local `-L`/third-party bundled libs in favor of system libraries. There is no network access, no download-and-execute, no obfuscation or encoding, no filesystem tampering, and no system modification. The change stays entirely within the package's own build configuration.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Benign qmake patch switching sioyek to system mupdf.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The supplied file is an Arch Linux AUR .SRCINFO metadata file and does not contain executable build logic or post-install behavior. It references the sioyek upstream Git repository and a patch, and it uses a SKIP checksum for the Git source while providing a SHA-256 checksum for the patch.

The Git source uses the mutable development branch rather than a pinned commit, which is a supply-chain hygiene concern and reduces reproducibility. However, the file content itself does not show malicious code, obfuscation, unauthorized downloads, data exfiltration, backdoors, or dangerous execution. No unambiguous malicious behavior was found, so the decision is SAFE for the provided file.
</details>
<evidence>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging conventions. The source array fetches the project's own upstream repository (github.com/ahrm/sioyek, matching the declared url) over https with a mutable development branch, which is normal for a -git package; the SKIP checksum is required practice for VCS sources, and the accompanying local patch has a real sha256sum.

The functions perform only routine operations: `pkgver()` uses git describe; `prepare()` applies the declared patch and runs a trivial sed tweak on a keybinding config file; `build()` runs qmake6 and make; `package()` installs into $pkgdir via make install plus install/cp of the app's own data files (tutorial.pdf, configs, man page, shaders). There are no unexpected network requests, no eval/base64/obfuscated commands, no git pull/fetch of unchecked content at build time, no modifications outside $pkgdir, and no data exfiltration or backdoor behavior.
</details>
